findings.title: Sender validation is bypassed when the Integration does not exist yet
findings.body: When Integration.objects.get() raises DoesNotExist, GitHubInstallation immediately calls pipeline.next_step() without comparing pipeline state 'github_authenticated_user' against the GitHub user who installed the app. That row is normally created asynchronously by the GitHub installation webhook, so completion races the webhook: a user who reaches this step before the webhook is processed (or if it is delayed/lost) finishes the pipeline and build_integration() creates the integration from the installation_id alone. This defeats the PR's stated guarantee that the authenticated GitHub user must match the app installer whenever the webhook has not already created the Integration.

findings.title: Sender check crashes for integrations whose metadata has no sender
findings.body: The new check unconditionally indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login']. Integrations created through this pipeline itself do not get a sender (build_integration only sets metadata['sender'] from state['sender'], which this pipeline never binds; test_basic_flow asserts metadata without 'sender'), and older integrations likewise may lack it. If such an Integration exists but has no OrganizationIntegration (e.g. the org link was removed and the installation is retried/moved to another org), installations_exist is False, this branch is reached, and a KeyError/TypeError produces a 500 instead of completing or showing the installation-failed page.

findings.title: Token exchange and user lookup exceptions escape as 500s instead of the failure page
findings.body: safe_urlopen() on line 423 is called outside the try/except (which only covers safe_urlread/parse_qsl), and get_user_info() on line 434 is also unguarded. A network error, timeout, or HTTP error from GitHub's token endpoint, or a failed /user request for a bad/expired token, will therefore raise out of OAuthLoginView.dispatch and return a 500. This contradicts the PR description that a wrong or reused 'code' (and by extension a failed token/user exchange) should show the 'Invalid installation request' error page.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The rewritten test's second request uses state 'ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05', which fails OAuthLoginView's pipeline-signature check before GitHubInstallation/build_integration ever queries GitHub for the installation. The assertion of 'Invalid installation request.' therefore passes via the state-mismatch branch, and the stubbed 404 from /app/installations/{id} and the 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' handling in build_integration are no longer covered by any test.
